learningObjectives.title: Source evaluation: origin, purpose, value and limitations (OPVL)

questions.q: In source analysis, OPVL stands for origin, purpose, value and:
questions.explain: OPVL evaluates a source's Origin, Purpose, Value and Limitations.

questions.q: The 'origin' of a source refers to:
options: Who produced it, when, and what type of source it is
questions.explain: Origin covers authorship, date and type, which shape how a source is interpreted.

questions.q: The 'purpose' of a source asks:
options: Why it was created and for what audience
questions.explain: Purpose considers the author's intention and intended audience.

questions.q: A 'limitation' of a source might be that it:
options: Is biased, one-sided or lacks key information
questions.explain: Limitations include bias, missing perspectives or restricted knowledge.

questions.q: A government propaganda poster is MOST valuable to a historian as evidence of:
options: Official attitudes and the messages authorities promoted
The private views of ordinary people
questions.explain: Propaganda reveals official messaging and intent, though it is limited as objective fact.

questions.q: Cross-referencing sources means:
options: Comparing sources to test consistency and reliability
questions.explain: Corroborating sources against each other helps assess reliability.

questions.q: A primary source is one that was:
options: Produced at the time of the events studied
Written centuries later by a textbook author
questions.explain: Primary sources originate from the period; secondary sources interpret it later.

questions.q: A secondary source is:
options: A later account that interprets or analyses events
A source from the exact time of the event
questions.explain: Secondary sources are produced after the event, often by historians.

questions.q: In 'The move to global war', Japan invaded Manchuria in:
questions.explain: Japan's invasion of Manchuria (1931) is a key event in the move to global war in East Asia.

questions.q: Germany remilitarised the Rhineland in:
questions.explain: Hitler's remilitarisation of the Rhineland (1936) breached the Treaty of Versailles.

questions.q: Appeasement of Hitler culminated in the 1938:
questions.explain: At Munich, Britain and France conceded the Sudetenland to Germany, a high point of appeasement.

questions.q: The League of Nations' response to Japanese aggression in Manchuria was:
options: Weak and ineffective, and Japan left the League
questions.explain: The League condemned Japan (Lytton Report) but could not enforce action; Japan withdrew.

questions.q: In 'Rights and protest', the US Supreme Court's Brown v. Board of Education (1954) ruled that:
questions.explain: Brown v. Board overturned 'separate but equal' in public schools.

questions.q: The Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955-56) was sparked by the arrest of:
questions.explain: Rosa Parks' arrest for refusing to give up her bus seat sparked the boycott.

questions.q: Martin Luther King Jr. is associated with a strategy of:
questions.explain: King advocated non-violent direct action in the US civil rights movement.

questions.q: Under 'Military leaders', Genghis Khan is known for founding:
questions.explain: Genghis Khan united the Mongol tribes and founded a vast empire.

questions.q: In 'Conquest and its impact', Hernan Cortes led the Spanish conquest of the:
questions.explain: Cortes led the conquest of the Aztec Empire in Mexico in the early 16th century.

questions.q: In 'Conflict and intervention', the 1994 Rwandan genocide was directed principally against the:
questions.explain: Hutu extremists carried out genocide against the Tutsi (and moderate Hutu) in 1994.

questions.q: When using a memoir written decades after the events it describes, a historian should be cautious because:
options: Memory and hindsight can affect its reliability
It must be a primary photograph
It cannot be used at all
questions.explain: Later memoirs may be shaped by faulty memory, hindsight or self-justification.

questions.q: Assessing the 'value and limitations' of a source with reference to its origin and purpose is central to:
questions.explain: OPVL-based evaluation is the core skill assessed in the Paper 1 source paper.
